questions.question: To react faster to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This lets you react faster to hazards.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, it should be:

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:

options.text: Stay in first gear.
Stay in neutral.
Stay in fifth gear.
Stay in any gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in first gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane for visibility.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as needed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side nearest the passing vehicle is safer.
You will experience more wind blast on the far side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may cause the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them.
Move to the shoulder to help them.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may tempt them to return too soon. The center position is safest.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always the right portion of the lane.
Is always the center portion of the lane.
Is always the left portion of the lane.
Changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as conditions change.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips again, then reapply the brake.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Avoid surface hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids other drivers' blind spots and surface hazards, and keeps an escape route open. Your position should not block your escape route.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually the same power as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.
Usually larger than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: You do not need extra following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
You cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
Traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when you cannot see the road ahead. Normal following distance is enough only when conditions are perfect.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Using the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Using both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: For maximum braking, apply both the front and rear brakes together. Neither wheel should lock up.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
Separate occasionally.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders should stay close together while leaving enough space to move safely. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Riding in pairs does not allow enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular and white with black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The drinker's body weight
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC depends on three things: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect their current BAC. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week. Regular pre-ride inspections help keep your motorcycle safe.

questions.question: When braking while turning:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it requires care. Your tire traction is partly used for the turn, so less is available for braking.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When riding at night, a motorcyclist should keep a minimum distance of:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is harder to see at night. Keep a three-second distance from the vehicle in front of you. This gives you more time to notice if they stop and to slow down or stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection during long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it muffles horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing loss, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs and other hearing protection prevent damage while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange for other transportation.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Slow their pace of drinking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can help prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, getting other friends involved to stop them, or slowing their drinking. Never suggest they drive on less-crowded roads—they should not drive at all if they have been drinking.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, make sure it has all of the following, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
Fits snugly.
Has no cracks or damage.
Looks attractive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How the helmet looks is not important for safety.
